correctness.rationale: Keep a witnessing tuple fixed, distinguishing the set W of its distinct values from the number k of slots. Enlarging a class with at least ell nonwitnesses cannot create a new pointed ell-diagram: all nonwitness values from that class in an assignment, including the new one, can be injected into the old nonwitness pool. Similarly, adding a new singleton when there are at least ell free classes creates no new diagram: an assignment meeting the new class uses at most ell-1 old free classes, leaving an unused one for the new value. Both moves preserve equality and equivalence with every variable, including repeated witnesses, and can be iterated without exhausting their premise. If neither applies there are at most |W| marked classes, at most ell-1 nonwitnesses per class, and at most ell-1 free classes, proving the stated bound. Induced restrictions retaining all witnesses give every smaller nonempty order at least |W|; one-point pumping covers every larger order, so the asserted tail from k+ell holds (it is not claimed as optimal). Sharpness uses k witnesses in different classes and forbids ell distinct nonwitnesses in one marked class, ell distinct elements of one free class, and ell different free classes. All three bans are expressible with just the ell universal slots. The displayed partition attains all caps simultaneously, and remains nonempty at k=0 since ell>=2. This is a universal symbolic proof; the frozen bounded checker and recorded outputs were inspected as supplementary evidence, not used as proof or executed.

evidence: The graph proof pumps via a homogeneous ell-set in one of 2^k witness-neighborhood profiles; its printed sufficient bound is 2^k*4^ell. The two-universal record covers exactly the first allowed ell. The RU1 and U1 results give finite model sizes, not cutoff sharpness.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For equivalence models the independent obstructions are a sufficiently populated class and a sufficient number of available free classes. Their simultaneous saturation supplies the exact endpoint; neither the graph Ramsey bound and its extremizers, nor a bounded minimum model size, yields this. The frozen mention of a published sharp all-graph endpoint was not established by the cited survey passage and is not used in the originality decision.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalence relations are partitions (or disjoint unions of cliques with reflexivity implicit). Rank-three truncation classifies complete bounded-rank theories without fixed witnesses, rather than finding an optimal largest model of a finite spectrum for every such pointed prefix. The ell=2 overlap does not give the higher-ell term or extremizers by substitution.

originality.rationale: Best of the inspected evidence, the uniform sharp endpoint k*ell+(ell-1)^2 for arbitrary ell is a substantive extension. The entire ell=2 statement, including its sharpness and tail, is already covered as a statement by a distinct Resultary record; no independent originality is credited for that case, and same-day dating provides no evidence of priority. Nor is general finite/cofinite behavior credited as new.
residual_risks: Pratt-Hartmann full text and the original 1930 Ramsey paper were not obtained. Graph sharpness is not verified from the survey; it is not needed for the assigned proof.
Earlier equivalent bounds may appear as partition-type arguments in unindexed literature, and priority for the overlapping ell=2 case is unresolved.

value.rationale: The quantitative endpoint for a natural fixed-prefix fragment with built-in equivalence is not supplied by general BSR dichotomy. A sharp threshold for all k and ell, with extremizers jointly saturating class-size and class-count constraints, is useful for bounding finite relative spectra. This judgment is about the uniform classification, not about recomputing the cataloged two-universal case or claiming an optimal starting point for the infinite tail.
